test_input: Hold RIGHT for 1 second, then LEFT for 1 second. Let the ball fall past the paddle. Press R to restart. Press ESC to quit.
expected_lose_output:
MOVE RIGHT
MOVE LEFT
GAME OVER
RESTART
QUIT
notes:
Controls and expected console prints:
- Left Arrow: prints "MOVE LEFT" when first pressed and moves the paddle left (Paddle script: game/paddle.gd).
- Right Arrow: prints "MOVE RIGHT" when first pressed and moves the paddle right (Paddle script: game/paddle.gd).
- R: when game is over, prints "RESTART" and restarts the game with score 0 (Main script: game/main.gd).
- Escape: prints "QUIT" and quits the game (Main script: game/main.gd).
Game rules and HUD:
- Score shown top-left as a Label and updated on each paddle bounce (Main script: game/main.gd).
- On ball-paddle bounce the ball emits a "bounced" signal (Ball script: game/ball.gd) which increments the score in main.gd.
- On miss (ball below the paddle) the ball emits a "missed" signal (game/ball.gd) and main.gd sets game state to gameover, prints "GAME OVER", displays "GAME OVER\nFinal Score: X" and stops the ball.
Implementation notes and limitations:
- All visuals use procedural drawing (ColorRect/Canvas drawing) per Plan; no external assets or sounds are used.
- Paddle squash is a quick scale change (game/paddle.gd squash()), visual only; it does not alter collision geometry.
- Ball spin is applied as velocity.x += paddle.velocity.x * 0.2 in game/ball.gd (an approximation of spin). The exact effect depends on paddle speed and is intentionally simplified.
- Window title is set via project.godot (config/name), not at runtime (project.godot). If platform overrides title behavior, the project name is used.
- Restart recreates paddle and ball scenes in place; all state (score, positions) are reset to initial values.

Files implementing controls and rules:
- game/main.gd: scene setup, HUD, score, game state, input actions, restart and quit handling.
- game/paddle.gd: paddle movement, edge clamping, input prints, squash animation.
- game/ball.gd: ball physics, wall and paddle collisions, spin application, bounce and miss signals.

Known engine/runtime constraints: designed for Godot 4; InputMap bindings are created at runtime in _ready().
